EVD-2397.description: July 2019 spot UT measurement on the 36" pipeline at the Gas Terminal area. Source records: "a reduction of thickness of 1.03mm along with heavy pitting and painting peeling off was observed in one of the segments of 36 pipeline in gas terminal in July 2019. The corrective action of painting was completed in Dec. 2019. However, as per the available data, the design thickness of the pipeline is 23.83mm with zero corrosion allowance. It needs to be examined whether painting as a corrective action would suffice in such cases and the mechanism of deciding on a corrective action needs to be reviewed" (p.30). 1.03 mm thickness reduction; designed thickness 23.83 mm; ZERO corrosion allowance. Heavy pitting + paint peeling. Corrective action: painting only (Dec 2019). Painting is a coating-restoration action; the underlying metal loss on a zero-allowance pipe was not evaluated for fitness-for-service — symptomatic vs root-cause treatment of corrosion.

EVD-2894.description: Pressure boundary integrity record: NO hydro test performed after 18-Sep-2020 gasket replacement. Source records: "After calibration of the meter 310FE01, the gasket was replaced on 18.09.2020. No hydro test was done after replacement of the gasket. The system was only pressurised to operating pressure (Both meters were in line) and isolated. Next day meter 310FE01 was taken on online and was in use at the time of Incident" (p.31). System pressurised only to operating pressure; standard pressure-boundary integrity test (hydro test to design pressure) not performed. The committee directly cites this as a contributing cause: "Probable cause of leak is due to use of nonstandard gasket and not testing the system to designed pressure. No standard operating procedure is in place for calibration and taking back in service of these meters which are operating at high pressures" (p.32).

EVD-9612.description: Witness statement of DGM (Production) - GSP Shift In-charge, called from quarters at ~02:35 hrs. Source records: "At around 0235 hrs, [DGM-GSP] received phone call from LPG Control Room and Gas Terminal control room, it was informed that heavy gas leakage near 36 metering area... [he] tried to enter the Gas Control room area but could not enter due to heavy gas smell. He informed Fire station to abstain from any vehicle movement in the plant... Further [DGM-GSP] closed the MOV 54 inlet condensate line from slug catcher to 36 metering area at about 0301 hrs. Thereafter fire occurred." (p.17). MOV 54 closure at 03:01 is 46 minutes after first physical detection (02:15) and 7 minutes before ignition (03:08:15). The shift in-charge had to physically reach Gas Terminal Gate before he could close the valve — the MOVs in the gas terminal station are not remote-operable from the control room during emergency (p.26).

EVD-6414.description: Reconstructed emergency response timeline — composite of CCTV, DCS, and witness statements. Source records the timeline (Section 5, pp.9-12; Section 9, pp.18-25): leak onset 02:12:50 (CCTV) -> first physical detection 02:15 (CISF perimeter) -> CISF-internal verification via CCTV 02:18 -> Gas Terminal CR notification 02:18-02:20 -> annunciator alarm 02:20 -> shift-in-charge phone call ~02:35 -> shift-in-charge reaches gate, MOV 54 closure 03:01 -> 36" PCV closure 03:04 -> ignition 03:08:15. Two critical intervals: 46 minutes from first detection to first isolation; 8 minutes from first isolation to ignition (the cloud already in the air ignited regardless of the eventual valve closures). The committee characterises this directly: "Decision of closure of valve was taken after about 40 minutes resulting the spread of vapour cloud in increased area" (p.32). The delay magnitude is the proximate response failure pattern; its roots are in escalation design and the DMP gap (row 46).

EVD-4052.description: On-site Disaster Management Plan (DMP) — hydrocarbon-leakage section omits isolation/stoppage decision criteria. Source records: "As per DMP On site Hazira Plant, guidelines to be followed in case of hydrocarbon leakage are included but does not include isolation/stoppage of facilities/pipelines" (p.32). Reinforced at p.27: "In ERDMP, scenario for Level 3 emergencies are taken from the plant failures. Heavy product/gas leakages from pipelines & tanks are considered but decision on isolation/closure of plant/pipelines is not mentioned." The DMP defines the scenario but not the decision: when does a hydrocarbon leak warrant unilateral pipeline isolation, and who has the authority to call it? This procedural gap directly correlates with the 46-minute response delay — personnel had no documented criterion to act on, and authority was concentrated above the shift-in-charge level (row 50). The committee's root cause #6 ("Non isolation/stoppage of 36 pipeline operation") flows from this finding.

EVD-3932.description: Plant organogram — night-shift authority chain reconstructed from witness statements (rows 1-7) and the committee's document review (p.18). Authority chain: perimeter (CISF Constable A) -> CCTV CR (CISF SI C) -> Gas Terminal CR (CE-P) -> GSP/LPG Shift In-charge (DGM-P) -> Overall Shift In-charge / SIC (GM-P) -> Resident Engineer (GM-P) + Head Operations (CGM-P) -> Plant Manager / CIC (GGM). Critical structural observation: NO role between Shift In-charge and Plant Manager has standing authority to close MOV 54 (or any other emergency-isolation valve) without telephoning up the chain — confirmed by the committee finding (p.26) that "MOVs are provided in the gas terminal station for local operations but they are not having remote operation from control room during emergency." The Overall Shift In-charge had to physically reach Gas Terminal Gate at ~02:35 and then "instructed closure" (row 7) — the operator at Gas Terminal Gate could not act unilaterally. Directly implicates the 46-minute first-detection-to-first-isolation gap. The escalation hierarchy was not designed for time-critical hydrocarbon containment.

EVD-8657.description: DCS annunciator panel record showing first alarm activation at the Gas Terminal Control Room at ~02:20 hrs. Source records: "At around 0220 hrs Mr. [CE] heard alarm on the annunciator panel" (p.17). Quantitative comparison: leak onset 02:12:50 (CCTV) -> human detection 02:15 (CISF) -> annunciator alarm 02:20. The automated detection lagged human detection by 5 minutes and lagged leak onset by ~7 minutes 10 seconds. The committee notes (p.26): "Hydrocarbon/H2S detectors are configured to Annunciator Panel for display but not in DCS for history" and "F&G detection system does not have provision for auto shut down of plant or activation of fire suppression system." The committee's recommendation A.1 at p.34 explicitly calls for: "F&G detection system needs to be interlocked to automatic plant shut down and activation of fire suppression system." This is the same gap that allowed the 46-minute pre-ignition response delay.

EVD-1394.description: Post-fire wide-angle photograph of the condensate metering skid area (1986-vintage installation, ground level, NW of Gas Terminal Control Room). Source describes the visible state at site inspection (5-8 Oct 2020, ~2 weeks post-fire): "the condensate metering skid was totally damaged & various pipelines have got damaged/shifted" (p.31). The skid superstructure was not designed to contain a flange-failure release — secondary damage propagation indicates inadequate barrier design.
